entries.title: II Chronicles 24:1
segments: ¶Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he was ruling for forty years in Jerusalem: his mother's name was Zibiah of Beer-sheba.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:2
segments: And Joash did what was right in the eyes of the Lord as long as Jehoiada the priest was living.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:3
segments: And Jehoiada took two wives for him, and he became the father of sons and daughters.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:4
segments: Now after this Joash had a desire to put the house of the Lord into good order again;

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:5
segments: And getting together the priests and Levites, he said to them, Go out into the towns of Judah year by year, and get from all Israel money to keep the house of your God in good condition; and see that this is done without loss of time. The Levites, however, were slow in doing so.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:6
segments: Then the king sent for Jehoiada, the chief priest, and said to him, Why have you not given the Levites orders that the tax fixed by Moses, the servant of the Lord, and by the meeting of Israel, for the Tent of witness, is to be got in from Judah and Jerusalem and handed over?

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:7
segments: For the house of the Lord had been broken up by Athaliah, that evil woman, and her sons; and all its holy things they had given to the Baals.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:8
segments: So at the king's order they made a chest and put it outside the doorway of the house of the Lord.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:9
segments: And an order was sent out through all Judah and Jerusalem that payment was to be made to the Lord of the tax which Moses, the servant of God, had put on Israel in the waste land.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:10
segments: And all the chiefs and all the people came gladly and put their money into the chest, till they had all given.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:11
segments: So when the chest was taken to the king's servants by the Levites, and they saw that there was much money in it, the king's scribe and the chief priest's servant took the money out, and put the chest back in its place. They did this day by day, and got together a great amount of money.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:12
segments: Then the king and Jehoiada gave it to those who were responsible for getting the work done on the Lord's house, and with it they got wall-builders and woodworkers and metal-workers to put the house of the Lord in good order again.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:13
segments: So the workmen did their work, making good what was damaged and building up the house of God till it was strong and beautiful again.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:14
segments: And when the work was done, they took the rest of the money to the king and Jehoiada, and it was used for making the vessels for the house of the Lord, all the vessels needed for the offerings, the spoons and the vessels of gold and silver. And as long as Jehoiada was living, the regular burned offerings were offered in the house of the Lord.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:15
segments: ¶But Jehoiada became old and full of days, and he came to his end; he was a hundred and thirty years old at the time of his death.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:16
segments: And they put him into his last resting-place in the town of David, among the kings, because he had done good in Israel for God and for his house.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:17
segments: Now after the death of Jehoiada, the chiefs of Judah came and went down on their faces before the king. Then the king gave ear to them.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:18
segments: And they gave up the house of the Lord God of their fathers, and became worshippers of pillars of wood and of the images; and because of this sin of theirs, wrath came on Judah and Jerusalem.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:19
segments: And the Lord sent them prophets to make them come back to him; and they gave witness against them, but they would not give ear.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:20
segments: Then the spirit of God came on Zechariah, the son of Jehoiada the priest, and, getting up before the people, he said to them, God has said, Why do you go against the orders of the Lord, so that everything goes badly for you? because you have given up the Lord, he has given you up.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:21
segments: But when they had made a secret design against him, he was stoned with stones, by the king's order, in the outer square of the Lord's house.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:22
segments: So King Joash did not keep in mind how good Jehoiada his father had been to him, but put his son to death. And in the hour of his death he said, May the Lord see it and take payment!

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:23
segments: Now in the spring, the army of the Aramaeans came up against him; they came against Judah and Jerusalem, putting to death all the great men of the people and sending all the goods they took from them to the king of Damascus.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:24
segments: For though the army of Aram was only a small one, the Lord gave a very great army into their hands, because they had given up the Lord, the God of their fathers. So they put into effect the punishment of Joash.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:25
segments: And when they had gone away from him, (for he was broken with disease,) his servants made a secret design against him because of the blood of the son of Jehoiada the priest, and they put him to death on his bed; and they put his body into the earth in the town of David, but not in the resting-place of the kings.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:26
segments: Those who made designs against him were Zabad, the son of Shimeath, an Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad, the son of Shimrith, a Moabite woman.

entries.title: II Chronicles 24:27
segments: Now the story of his sons, and all the words said by the prophet against him, and the building up again of the Lord's house, are recorded in the account in the book of the kings. And Amaziah his son became king in his place.
